title: Channel and Parallel.ForEachAsync
cards/0/body:
A Channel<T> is an async queue: some code writes with WriteAsync, other code reads with ReadAllAsync.

A bounded channel (CreateBounded) makes a fast producer wait until the consumer catches up. This is backpressure.
cards/1/q: A channel with room for 100 items is full. What does WriteAsync do?
cards/1/explain: That's the default behavior (BoundedChannelFullMode.Wait). Dropping items happens only if you ask for it explicitly.
cards/2/options/0: So a fast producer doesn't fill up memory when the consumer can't keep up
cards/2/explain: With no limit, the queue can grow until memory runs out.
cards/3/body: Since .NET 6 you can process a collection asynchronously with a concurrency limit. It won't fire off 10,000 requests at once.
cards/4/q: You need to download 10,000 files, at most 8 at a time. What do you pick?
cards/4/explain: WhenAll over 10,000 tasks will swamp the server, and a sequential loop will take forever.
cards/5/q: Which are true? Select all that apply.
cards/5/options/0: A Channel is an async queue between parts of a program
cards/5/options/1: A bounded channel gives you backpressure
cards/5/options/2: Parallel.ForEachAsync limits the number of concurrent operations
cards/5/options/4: A Channel stores data on disk
cards/5/explain: WhenAll waits for everything you give it; limiting is up to you.
cards/6/explain: No more than 8 downloads at a time.
cards/7/pairs/1/1: A queue with a limit and waiting
cards/7/pairs/2/1: Read until the channel is closed
cards/7/pairs/3/1: Process a collection with a limit
